segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Of that same year:
and after a week of days he was killed.
Now Namiqa {OCR?} also, the Persian,
who had already slandered Aruq,
and that he was going to extract a hundred myriad (one million) dinkars {OCR?: dirhams / dinars} from the kings, rulers, and scribes whom Aruq had appointed in the provinces,
those who had oppressed and taken without right,
and had devastated the provinces.
Therefore, on account of the hatred towards Aruq, his word was accepted,
and an evil decree went out against them.
And their affair was handed over to Amir Baytmish,
so that when 'Abd al-Mu'min made the audit of these,
whatever was found against them,
he, Baytmish, should take back from them by blows and torments,
and put to death without mercy anyone who was guilty of death.
And because Mas'ud son of Qawti, his brothers, and his relatives did not know anyone in the royal camp except Buqa,
and they considered the service of other amirs to be vanity,
and they did not deign even to offer a bare greeting to those others;
and because Buqa's command was high and exalted over all the amirs,
they neglected them all,
and attached themselves to Buqa alone,
even though they were constantly rebuked and blamed by everyone for this.
And they used to give them counsel,
saying: "It is not right to neglect the service, submission, and compliance towards those amirs who are constant in the royal service,
and to attach oneself to one and alienate {OCR?: offend} many is a despicable deed;
for it is possible that some trial may happen to that one amir upon whom you have relied,
and you will not be helped by the others."
Now that Mas'ud,
because he was childish in his mind and not prudent in his conduct,
used to say in boastfulness:
"I do not desire life without Buqa,
and if Buqa should die,
is death better for me, or life?"
Which indeed came to pass,
and his word proved true {OCR?: turned out to the letter}.
For on the very day that Aruq was seized,
they set guards over Mas'ud and guarded him carefully,
until 'Abd al-Mu'min and Namiqa {OCR?} the Persian arrived.
Then persecution and wrath were stirred up against the envied Christians,
and, that I may not say [worse],
an abandonment by God.
And they began to torment them without mercy;
they tormented most especially Taj al-Din bar Mukhtas,
